elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase, service, or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Customer remains required to obtain all Services included in the Monthly Base Fee during the stated twelve-month period, and subsection (ii) expressly retains a minimum monthly fee.

elements.element: Fees are charged only for Services actually used or affirmatively ordered by Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause retains a minimum Monthly Base Fee for bundled Services and requires Customer to obtain all included Services, rather than limiting charges to actual usage or Services affirmatively ordered.

elements.element: Any minimum commitment is limited to the current 12-month term and does not create liability beyond that period.
elements.evidence: Although Section A substitutes a 'then-current twelve (12) month period,' that period is not defined or anchored and may recur throughout the Term. More importantly, Estimated Remaining Value continues to be calculated through the last day of the full Term using the Monthly Base Fee and other minimum monthly fees.

elements.element: Customer may reduce or discontinue committed Services on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The added sentence expressly permits Customer, upon 30 days' notice to M&I, to reduce or discontinue any Service included in the Monthly Base Fee.

elements.element: Following a reduction or discontinuation, the applicable fee is adjusted through a true-up reflecting the reduced usage or Services.
elements.evidence: The added sentence requires the Monthly Base Fee to be equitably reduced to reflect resource units no longer used and expressly characterizes the adjustment as a true-up.

elements.element: No shortfall penalty or economically equivalent remaining-term minimum charge applies to the commitment.
elements.evidence: The added sentence disclaims a shortfall penalty for Service reductions, but the retained Estimated Remaining Value formula preserves an economically similar remaining-term calculation based on minimum monthly fees through the last day of the full Term.

result.reason: The redline adds the requested notice and true-up mechanics, but it does not fully implement either position. Minimum fees and mandatory bundled Services remain, defeating the preferred position. The retained full-Term Estimated Remaining Value formula, together with the undefined and potentially recurring 'then-current' twelve-month period, prevents a clear 12-month cap and preserves a remaining-term charge inconsistent with the fallback's no-penalty requirement. The non-operative margin comment does not cure those defects.
